I will keep my land in the usual Quzhou pattern of winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is the system I trust most here because it fits the climate, the irrigation conditions, and the market, and at my age I value a steady, manageable plan over chasing higher-risk crops. I am educated enough to use improved seed, soil testing habits, and tighter input control, so I will aim for stable yield rather than maximum input. For wheat, I will use improved seed, plough after the previous crop residue is managed, apply balanced nitrogen with moderate phosphorus and potassium, irrigate at the key stages, and keep pesticide sprays limited to what is needed for weeds, aphids, rust, and other disease pressure. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize with hybrid seed, rotary tillage to save time, a higher nitrogen rate than wheat, and fewer irrigations because the rainy season helps. I will manage both crops conservatively, keep field operations timely, and avoid unnecessary passes so the work stays efficient and realistic for me.
